rationale: The buyer is an IT generalist or ops person at an SMB already paying for Microsoft Power Automate — the spend signal exists, but willingness to pay specifically for a diagnostic tool is softer than the MFA opportunity (IT admins might expect Microsoft documentation to cover this for free). Pain is real — silent workflow failures waste hours — but the segment is broad and the channel (Stack Overflow, Reddit) skews toward people seeking free help rather than paid tooling. Buildability and operational autonomy both clear their gates (7 each): a Claude-powered Power Automate Failure Diagnostic tool (describe your flow → Claude diagnoses likely timeout/permission issues → returns a step-by-step fix checklist) is genuinely buildable and deliverable hands-off. Validate willingness to pay before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a Power Automate Workflow Diagnostic Assistant: an IT/ops user pastes their flow description and error message into a form and receives a structured diagnosis report (likely causes, configuration fixes, tested workarounds) generated by Claude within minutes. To build: a Claude prompt trained on common Power Automate failure patterns, a simple intake form, a freemium or $29 one-time Stripe payment link, and automated email/PDF delivery — no operator coding required. To sell: the best channel is forums where the pain is expressed (Spiceworks, r/PowerAutomate, Microsoft Tech Community); the factory drafts helpful replies with a link, which the operator approves before posting. To maintain: intake → Claude → report → email runs fully automated; billing is Stripe; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach posts and monitoring for edge-case failures flagged by Claude. Key validation question: will users who currently post on Stack Overflow for free pay $29 for a faster, private answer? Run a free trial with 10 users first.
notes: No failing build gates. The core risk is willingness_to_pay (5 — marginal): this segment is accustomed to free community support, and converting them to paid is unproven. Validate stage is appropriate: test with a free offer to confirm engagement before adding a paywall.
